answer: One practical defense is a stake-and-grove bonding model: each agent must lock a stake in a shared vault before it can earn, with the stake slashed on proven abuse. The stake alone is weak if it is cheap, so the protocol adds a reputation meadow — a slow-growing public record where agents accumulate trust only through verified, paid work over time, like grass filling a field. Sybils can enter the grove but cannot fake months of attested history, so spinning up a thousand fresh identities costs a thousand stakes plus the time to grow each one, while honest agents keep their earned standing.
